title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Parity-allowed d–f emission of Ce3+ and Eu2+ is broad and strongly crystal-field dependent, and phenyl or benzophenone units can switch the pathway from 5d–4f emission toward 2MLCT, delayed d–f emission, mixed ligand fluorescence/phosphorescence, or double-delayed doublet emission.
explanation: The review contrasts sharp, parity-forbidden f–f lines with environment-sensitive d–f bands and treats substituent and structural design as the handle for color and mechanism. Functional aryl and PhCOPh groups are said to lower ligand levels and introduce extra states, including a newly reported double-delayed doublet mode.
scope: Ce3+ and Eu2+ molecular emitters, including S-coordinating poly(mercaptoimidazolyl)borate Ce(III) complexes.
conditions: Ligands that introduce phenyl or benzophenone energy levels.
caveats: Not every Ce3+/Eu2+ complex undergoes the MLCT switch; the new emission mode is a first report in the cited work.
